title: Stochastic Signal Firmament
content:
Goal: quick personal scratchpad for experiments that modulate stochasticity as a signal channel rather than noise. Exploring how temperature / top-p / seed jitter can be used as an intentional steering knob in a small prompt library and cataloging brittle failure modes.

High-level idea (brain dump):
- Treat sampling hyperparams (temp, top_p, typical_p) as a dimension of prompt templates.
- Encode a 3-way instruction set: deterministic baseline (temp=0.0), balanced (temp=0.6), exploratory (temp=1.0).
- Use few-shot exemplars that are explicitly labeled with the sampling regime so the model knows which style to mimic.

Quick hypotheses:
1) Explicitly labeling the exemplar with the intended sampling regime reduces cross-contamination (exemplar dominance).
2) High temp exemplars improve creative paraphrase but increase hallucination rate for factual tasks.
3) For short-token slot-filling, even small increases in temp produce inconsistent slot markers ("<slot>").

Prototype few-shot set (3 exemplars) — format: [REGIME] EXAMPLE => EXPECTED
- [DETERMINISTIC] Q: Convert: "Jan 2 2023" to ISO date. A: 2023-01-02
- [BALANCED] Q: Rewrite concisely: "Due to the fact that we observed an anomaly, we are postponing." A: We postponed due to an anomaly.
- [EXPLORATORY] Q: Generate 3 subject-line ideas for a product update about speed improvements. A: "Zoom into faster: product update", "Your apps, 2x faster — rollout notes", "Speed matters: behind the scenes of our latency cuts"

Sample prompt template (working):
"You are an assistant that obeys the sampling tag. RESPOND in the style of [REGIME].
EXEMPLARS:
{few_shot_examples}
USER: {user_input}
REGIME: [BALANCED]
OUTPUT:"

Observed quick failure cases (notes):
- "Instruction erosion": when exemplar and user regimes mismatch the model sometimes ignores the regime line. Adding a short chitchat line ("Reply in the style specified above.") helped in 2/5 runs.
- "Exemplar dominance": long, very specific exemplars push output to repeat phrasing even when regime is different. Shorten exemplars or add explicit "Do not copy phrasing" admonition.
- "Tokenization gotchas": emojis used as bullet anchors (✅) cause different token counts across models; affects prefix caching and sequence length heuristics. Avoid emoji anchors for deterministic tasks.
- "Slot drift": when using annotated slots e.g., <name>: the model will sometimes render "Name:" if temperature>0.7. Consider using unique unicode separators (▁) or token sequences unlikely in natural text.

Experiment matrix (short):
- Vars: temp (0.0, 0.3, 0.6, 1.0), top_p (0.9 vs 1.0), exemplar length (short vs long), regime-label present vs absent.
- Metrics: exact_match (slot tasks), BLEU/ROUGE for paraphrase proxies, hallucination_rate (manual binary sample), diversity (distinct n-grams).
- Runs: 50 samples per cell, seed sweep [42, 73, 101], model variants: redwood-tiny-test (local smoke), redwood-1.0-beta (hosted).

Quick-run notes / commands (scratch):
- Local smoke: python run_prompt_playground.py --model redwood-tiny-test --temp 0.6 --shots 3 --seed 42 --payload-file ./toy-cases.json
- Hosted check: curl -X POST $REDWOOD_API/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0-beta","input":"<templated prompt>","temperature":0.6}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

Failure case examples to capture in test-suite (for PR):
- FC-1: Label ignored when exemplar contains contradictory wording (e.g., label BALANCED, exemplar phrased like EXPLORATORY).
- FC-2: Named slot fragmented across tokens when temp>0.5 (example: "<city>New York</city>" -> "<c ity>New York</city>"). Likely tokenization/byte-level bug or sampling-induced split.
- FC-3: Excessive deterministic repetition with temperature 0.3 for paraphrase task when exemplar contains template phrase.

Mitigations tried (notes):
- Hard separators + explicit "DO NOT ECHO" line reduced verbatim repetition in 60% of tests.
- Inserted gating instruction between exemplars and user prompt ("--- end exemplars ---"). Sometimes decreases exemplar influence.
- Explicit regime anchor at the beginning of exemplar ("[REGIME: BALANCED]") seems more stable than trailing regime lines.

Next steps / TODO:
- [ ] Formalize a 20-case dataset for the most common FCs and add to prompt-regression harness. Link to JIRA (PROMPT-87).
- [ ] Add variant with unicode-heavy separators and measure slot drift.
- [ ] Try kv-cache-aware prefixes to see if caching interacts with regime anchors (esp. across batched requests).
- [ ] Write short doc for Solutions/SEs: "Using sampling as a signal: do's and don'ts" (one-pager).

Random notes / stray thoughts:
- Could we exploit temp variation as an implicit style token (i.e., train a small RL head that maps intent -> temp)? Risky but may be useful for product UIs that expose a single slider.
- Some enterprise customers will want deterministic outputs but also creativity on demand; having canonical "regime tags" could be a simple contract we expose via API.

References / links I kept in my head:
- convo in #prompt-harvest: thread id 23345 (Jordan) where we discussed exemplar length tradeoffs.
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-playground/pull/312 (early harness for sampling matrix).

Scratch examples to keep (for tests):
1) Slot fill: prompt -> "Extract customer name and city from: 'Order placed by Maya Reed, 12 Baker St, Toronto'". Expected: {"name":"Maya Reed","city":"Toronto"}
2) Paraphrase: prompt -> "Shorten: 'We have made an improvement to reduce system latency by up to 40% in common read paths.'". Expected: 'We cut latency ~40% on common read paths.'
3) Creative subject lines: prompt -> "Write 5 subject lines for release notes about a performance patch". Expect variety, measure distinct n-grams.

Keep iterating. This doc is messy by design — quick capture for later extraction into proper test-cases and one-pager.

Notes-to-self: when I extract tests, prefer to store inputs and canonical outputs in csv (id,input,regime,expected) to avoid nested json in our harness.

End of notes.
